terra.problem: Calling the Teacher king in Jerusalem introduces a fact from Ecclesiastes 1:12 without a reference to that verse.
The passage does not say whether the king had a sidekick.
The passage credits the man's wisdom with saving the city but does not say whether an army was involved.
The passage does not say that nobody picked up a sling.
Being forgotten does not establish that the man received no parade.
The passage does not say the man was forgotten by the end of the day.
The passage does not establish that there were no scribes with scrolls.
The passage does not say that no gold changed hands.
The verse does not say how quickly the good is destroyed.
The image says the dead flies bring a stench to the oil, not that a few flies spoil a whole jar.
It guesses what the fool would love without marking it as a guess. The passage also does not say that nothing stays hidden on the road.
The verse contrasts the strength needed for a dull axe with the success skill produces. It does not compare skill with size.
The verse calls the wise man's words gracious but does not say honor belongs with them.
The passage says the beginning of the talk is folly; it does not specify the first word.
Not knowing the way to the city does not establish that the fool is trying and failing to find his destination.
The explanation is generic and simply supplies the verse, with little of Papa Dorin's personality.
